statement: The function $f$ has domain $-2 \le x \le 6$ and range $1 \le y \le 5$. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = -f(x + 3) + 2$. What is the range of $g$?

choices.misconception: I shifted the domain $-2 \le x \le 6$ three units left and gave that new domain instead of the range.
I added the $2$ before applying the negative sign, so I computed $-(1 + 2)$ and $-(5 + 2)$.
I ignored the negative sign in front of $f$ and just added $2$ to the range $1 \le y \le 5$.

hints: A horizontal shift changes inputs only. It cannot change the outputs.
$f(x + 3)$ still takes every value from $1$ to $5$. Negate those outputs, then add $2$, and put the new endpoints in order.
Negating gives $-5 \le y \le -1$. Now add $2$ to both ends.

solutions.reliable: The inside shift $x + 3$ moves the graph left but leaves the set of outputs unchanged, so $f(x + 3)$ has range $1 \le y \le 5$. Multiplying by $-1$ flips this to $-5 \le y \le -1$. Adding $2$ gives $-3 \le y \le 1$. So the range of $g$ is $-3 \le y \le 1$.
solutions.elegant: Track the extreme outputs: the largest output $5$ of $f$ becomes $-5 + 2 = -3$, and the smallest output $1$ becomes $-1 + 2 = 1$.
